newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania presidential vote set for December 21.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania presidential vote set for December 21.

text.p: Lithuania is to hold presidential elections on December 21, expected to pit incumbent Algirdas Brazauskas against arch-rival Vytautas Landsbergis, parliament's protocol office said on Thursday.
It will be the second presidential race since the Baltic state quit the former Soviet Union in 1991.
Brazauskas is former head of the Soviet-era Lithuanian Communist Party, who led a break from the main Moscow-dominated party and began the Baltic state's quest for independence.

He is expected to be re-elected if he decides to run. But has not yet said he will stand. Political commentators expect him to run, saying the burly 64-year-old relishes his role as leader of the country and enjoys a political fight.
Despite his communist past, Brazauskas, president since 1993, has a solid pro-reform reputation and is a staunch supporter of joining both NATO and the European Union.

Six candidates have announced they will enter the race but the contenders with the most chance are independence hero Landsbergis and U.S. emigre Valdus Adamkus, a former official of the U.S. Environment Protection Agency.
Landsbergis, who spearheaded Lithuania's independence movement and confronted Moscow, now heads a resurgent right-wing in Lithuania.

His Homeland Union party swept to power in parliamentary elections in late 1996. Capturing the presidency would seal a political comeback for Landsbergis, a former music professor who is chairman of parliament.
Adamkus, proposed by the third-largest party in parliament, the Centre Union, has been trying to boost his image in Lithuania and leads Landsbergis in opinion polls.
